frozen_note: Pairs are declared before data. After-state semantics: REPAIR pairs are green when the statement RE-READ at <lands> (statement_after, LAST occurrence) equals the lands observation and differs from the base statement (round-73 statement_after idiom: re-read token != base token AND the base stated_text absent from the file at <lands>); ANNOTATE pairs stay as filed and are closed by a '## Corrections — round 74' row naming id + old token + new token + the re-derivation command, which the counter re-runs and must return the new token. pair_semantics.id: unique pair id; LC-04, LC-05, LC-13, LC-14 are retired (deleted_pairs) and LC-10 was dropped for a guard incompatibility (dropped_candidates); none may be reused
pair_semantics.stated_at: path:line in the BASE tree, or fleet:<path>:<line> with a stated_fleet block
pair_semantics.stated_text: verbatim substring of that line at the base revision
pair_semantics.stated_parse: regex with exactly one capture group, applied to stated_text, yielding the STATED token
pair_semantics.observe_cmd: argv list; argv[0] in {git, grep, wc, sha256sum, ls, cat, head, tail, cut}; validated by the counter's H2 guard (allowlist, read-only git subcommand, no interpreter, no shell metacharacter, every operand resolving in the clone)
pair_semantics.parse: regex with exactly one capture group applied to observe_cmd stdout, yielding the OBSERVED token
pair_semantics.expected_after: the token the counter must observe at <lands> by re-running observe_cmd (base-pinned argvs are lands-invariant by construction)
pair_semantics.observed_at_base: the token measured by running observe_cmd at base on 2026-10-25 through the counter's own run_observe in a base clone
pair_semantics.red_at_base: stated token != observed token (a green pair must be dropped, never listed)
pair_semantics.disposition: REPAIR (live statement, edited at <lands>) or ANNOTATE (filed history, closed by a SCORECARD correction row)
pair_semantics.statement_after: REPAIR only: {path, parse} - the repaired statement is re-read with the DOTALL last-occurrence idiom and must capture expected_after
pair_semantics.rederive: the same observation as one human-runnable command line (shlex-split; the counter re-runs the argv form)

grammar_requirements.rule: Absence semantics for `git grep -c`: exit 1 with empty stdout means ZERO matches and yields the token "0". Scope it to argv whose argv[0:2] are git/grep and which carry -c or -l. NO pair in this ledger uses it (the four absence pairs were deleted); it is retained because the RECEIPTS leg and any future round need the class, and the draft counter already implements it in _absence_observation.
grammar_requirements.why: Pre-freeze L1 + RevClaimsFidelity F3/F4 removed the absence pairs; the absence is now carried by the RECEIPTS leg alone.

grammar_requirements.rule: Observe allowlist = {git, grep, wc, sha256sum, ls, cat, head, tail, cut}. No interpreter, no echo/printf/true-style constant printer, no shell metacharacter (| & ; < > ` $( newline) in any argv element. Counts use `git diff --shortstat <empty-tree> <rev> -- '<glob>'` (prints 'N files changed') or `git grep -c`. Registry-row counts use the pipe-free regex `^. S[0-9]{3}` (measured identical to the claims' own row regex at 804 / 724 / 752 on the three revisions used) so no re-derivation command carries a pipe inside a markdown table cell.
grammar_requirements.why: Round-73 routed defect 4 (ledger constant-printers). The guard also refuses `>` anywhere in an argv element, which is why LC-11's regex is written `decompress.*23443.*[0-9]+ bytes` instead of containing an ASCII arrow.

grammar_requirements.rule: Revision discipline: an argv that must CHANGE between base and lands reads the graded tree; an argv that must NOT move pins its revision as a FULL 40-hex operand (the git-grep guard accepts only 40-hex or HEAD as a revision operand, and a 7-hex abbreviation is refused as a mutable-ref/path). Every pair here pins what it observes, so landing claim C cannot move a Ca observation: the SEPARABLE hazard.
grammar_requirements.why: The three revision-block pairs name the landing commit they are about as a full 40-hex AND the pinned base, because the ANNOTATE leg requires the base revision as an operand of every numeric pair.

grammar_requirements.rule: Statement re-reads (statement_after, and any 'latest value' read) take the LAST occurrence in the file, via the DOTALL `(?s).*PATTERN` idiom or findall()[-1]. Fixture: a file with two 'Total knowledge entries:' lines, the first stale.
